messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx spike (500, 502) for eu-central on provider-blue starting 2026-03-15T09:00:30Z. error-rate 18% for generation endpoints. auto-remediation attempted (scale-up) failed. paging ops-oncall and sre roster.

ops-oncall: taking it. oncall here — will triage, please @ajay @maria for routing+rate-limit help. any customer P1s?

ajay: seeing increased tail latency + token dropouts. provider-blue reports intermittent network flaps. throughput to eu-west unaffected. suspect provider-side packet loss causing connection resets to our runtime.

maria: confirmed. traffic shaping queues spiking on blue instances. KV-cache hit rates normal. no obvious model regressions.

sophie: tagging CS to surface any live customer complaints. @elaine-cs?

elaine-cs: we have two customers reporting higher error rates for chat streams. No legal/regulatory P1s yet. they requested realtime ETA.

carl: quick mitigation plan: 1) emergency route ~20-30% of eu-central traffic to provider-green (compatible region) via weighted routing, 2) apply short-term rate limits for anonymous/low-tier tokens, 3) brownout non-essential streaming features for impacted routes, 4) prepare region failover if things degrade.

ajay: agree. I'll run a conservative provider-reroute to start: route 25% to provider-green and keep 75% on blue. watch for error-rate delta.

maria: while ajay runs reroute, I'll push a throttling rule for free-tier keys and new sessions: 25 QPS -> 10 QPS for 30m and bump back if stable. also disable streaming-chunked for non-enterprise routes.

ops-oncall: do we want to disable realtime streaming for enterprise? that'd be visible to customers — prefer not unless forced. do lite brownout for public routes only.

ajay: starting reroute now. command:

```\n# redwoodctl route update --region eu-central --policy weighted \\\n--weights provider-blue=75,provider-green=25 --note "emergency partial reroute due to blue network flaps"\n```

ajay: done. config pushed. monitoring: new TS 09:03:12 shows initial shift, error-rate for blue target decreased slightly; green error-rate currently 2%. overall 5xx down to 12% from 18%.

maria: applying temporary quota change:

```\n# redwoodctl quota adjust --scope public --region eu-central --limit 10rps --duration 30m --reason "emergency rate cap"\n```

maria: quota pushed. adding traffic-shaping rule to deprioritize long-lived streaming sessions older than 60s for non-paid keys. brownout toggle: streaming=false for /v1/stream endpoints for tier=public.

carl: adding a short-term circuit on the experimental 'fast-mode' feature for generation to avoid extra open sockets.

ops-oncall: posting an internal comms snippet for CS and Sales: "Experiencing provider network flaps in eu-central. Partial reroute in progress. Some free-tier streaming may be degraded. Enterprise customers on dedicated capacity unaffected unless routed to provider-blue." please review and push to statuspage if we hit 15%+ error for 5m.

elaine-cs: ack. prepping customer messages for impacted accounts, will prioritize top 3 paying customers and offer mitigation steps.

sophie: monitoring dashboards: request latency tail improving at 09:06, but we see occasional spikes when routing changes land. no new deploys.

ajay: next step if errors rebound: increase weight to provider-green to 60% and consider full provider cutover for blue in eu-central. also start draining blue pool:

```\n# redwoodctl pool drain --provider provider-blue --region eu-central --grace 300\n```

luca (via DM to ops-oncall): can you pre-authorize failover for provider-green? want to ensure no billing hurdles.

ops-oncall: pre-authorized for this incident. finance notified.

maria: within 20m we saw error-rate drop to 6%. streaming brownout reduced support churn. public-tier errors down to <5%.

incident-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-141 created and auto-populated with metrics snapshot and runbook link.

ajay: heads-up — we're seeing a new class of 502s coming from long-tail connections on provider-green at 09:23. probably different root cause. temporarily pausing increase to green. reverting weights back to 50/50 to avoid cascading.

carl: ok switching to shaping-only mode: keep weights 50/50, tighten new-session token limits and extend streaming brownout another 30m.

ops-oncall: doing a warm-handoff — my shift ends in 15m. @sophie you'll take secondary oncall; i'll leave a summary with actionables.

sophie: taking it. summary pls in one line.

ops-oncall: SUMMARY: partial provider reroute (blue->green 25%), public-tier rate-limits lowered to 10rps, streaming brownout for non-paid routes, monitoring for error-rate rebound. watch metrics: eu-central 5xx, provider-blue net errors. TODO: if 5xx > 10% for 5m -> increase green weight to 60% then drain blue.

ajay: documenting commands used and rollback steps in thread.

elaine-cs: sent customer notices to top 3. one replied asking for ETA — told them 30-45m and mitigation steps.

sophie: continuing watch. at 09:48 error-rate stable ~4%. will remain on rotation for next hour, then coordinate with infra to run post-incident analysis.

maria: scheduling followup: run a quick eval on gateway timeouts and edge retry behavior for provider-blue. logging enabled for 5xx cases.

incident-bot: Update: metrics stable for 30m. incident status: mitigated. please file postmortem with timeline and decisions.

ops-oncall: thanks team. handing off to @sophie for follow-up. :wave:

sophie: will own postmortem. quick notes: feature brownout prevented larger customer impact; weighted routing avoided full failover and gave breathing room. main action items: 1) confirm provider SLA telemetry, 2) improve auto-fallback thresholds, 3) add targeted synthetic tests for provider-blue.

carl: created a ticket (INFRA-872) for improving reroute automation thresholds and a followup (PM-411) for customer-facing playbook updates.

elaine-cs: customers updated and offered credits where appropriate. no escalations.

sophie: closing thread. leaving incident ticket open for postmortem until next week. thanks all. :thumbsup:
